items.title: Ridgeway Plaza could get 4-storey parking garage, Mississauga mayoral candidates say
items.summary: The idea of building a four-storey parking garage to help solve well-documented problems at an embattled plaza in the city’s west end was floated on Friday afternoon at a Mississauga mayoral candidates debate. Responding to a question from the moderator near the end of the debate that asked the four main candidates what they’d do to make Ridgeway Plaza — home to some 115 restaurants — more pedestrian- and traffic-friendly, incumbent Carolyn Parrish was the first to speak. Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 to succeed a provincial politics-bound Bonnie Crombie, immediately pointed to a “large plot of land” behind Ridgeway Plaza, which opened in 2022. ” Parking garage “will pay for itself in three to four years” With people paying to park, “the parking facility will pay for itself in three to four years. ” While the quartet of mayoral hopefuls — the lineup also included city councillors Alvin Tedjo (Ward 2) and Dipika Damerla (Ward 7) — spent most of the nearly two-hour debate at the Sheridan College Hazel McCallion Campus in the city’s downtown core disagreeing on numerous issues of importance to Canada’s seventh-largest city, they did agree, for the most part, on a new parking garage at Ridgeway Plaza. Crombie, Mississauga’s mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to take the reins of Ontario’s Liberal Party, told those in attendance at the election season’s first mayoral debate in the city that she’s concerned for residents living near the huge west-end plaza who’ve dealt with noise and other issues in recent years.

items.title: People can see this natural ‘phenomenon’ in the Credit River in Mississauga
items.summary: It’s been called one of nature’s most amazing feats, and it takes place this time of year in Mississauga and several other places across the Greater Toronto Area. And for those who know where to go for the best up-close look, the salmon run, which the City of Mississauga has called an “annual phenomenon,” is said to be an unforgettable experience as thousands of fish swim upstream in the river from Lake Ontario. The annual salmon run, or migration, gets underway each September in the Credit River in Mississauga — and in parts of Brampton and Caledon — and continues through the end of October. Among the best places in the city to witness the natural event, historically, are Erindale Park, The Riverwood Conservancy’s Riverwood Park and Meadowvale Conservation Area. City of Mississauga officials each year encourage residents of all ages to bear witness to the salmon run, which the city notes usually peaks in early October. ” As Mississauga officials have also explained, the salmon during the late summer and early fall each year “push their way against the current of the Credit River to spawn and lay their eggs, and it all happens right here in Mississauga. As water temperatures start to cool and water levels deepen thanks to fall rains, freshwater salmon begin their yearly trek from the mouth of Lake Ontario up the Credit River to spawn.

items.title: City Weighs a Second 'Signature Park' Just North of Kariya Park in Mississauga's Downtown Core
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga is exploring plans for what staff describe as a possible second signature park in the city's downtown core, just steps north of the existing Kariya Park. City staff wrote in a report going to council on Tuesday that the new greenspace could become a distinctive and memorable public space and a focal point for residents and visitors in the Downtown Core. The proposed site sits at the corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive, though at just under one acre it would be significantly smaller than Kariya Park itself. Raj Sheth, the city's commissioner of community services, said in the report that the new park's proximity to Kariya Park, already regarded as one of the city's most treasured public spaces, offers a chance to complement and enhance the broader park experience in that part of downtown. Staff are recommending the city enter into a memorandum of understanding with developer Camrost Felcor to explore an enhanced park design for the city-owned property at that southwest corner, according to INsauga. The greenspace under consideration sits adjacent to a site Camrost Felcor is currently developing.

items.title: Weekly Yard Waste Pickup Returns This Fall as Peel Region Preps a Bigger Service Handoff to Brampton
items.summary: According to INsauga, weekly yard waste pickup is set to begin again this fall across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, with residents able to check their own collection calendar or sign up for free reminders to find their pickup day. Acceptable yard waste includes leaves, yard rakings with debris, tree trimmings and branches, brush and hedge clippings, household and garden plants, and Halloween pumpkins without the candle, INsauga reports. The outlet notes grass clippings are not accepted either at the curb or at Community Recycling Centres, and all yard waste at the curb must go in kraft paper bags or reusable containers clearly marked as yard waste, since plastic bags are not accepted. Looking further ahead, INsauga reports that starting in October of next year, the City of Brampton will take over garbage, organics and yard waste collection for both Brampton and Caledon, a service currently handled by the Region of Peel. According to INsauga, that shift is part of a broader provincial restructuring of services across Peel Region that is moving several responsibilities from the regional government to Brampton, Caledon and Mississauga.

items.title: Attempted Murder Charge Upgraded to Second-Degree Murder After Labour Day Stabbing Victim Dies
items.summary: According to INsauga, a Mississauga woman now faces a second-degree murder charge after the victim of a Labour Day weekend stabbing died in hospital four days after the attack. Peel Regional Police say officers responded to a stabbing in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East in the city's east end and found a man with a serious stab wound to the neck, who was taken to hospital in critical condition. INsauga reports the stabbing happened outside a shelter on Dundas Street near Main Street, several blocks east of Dixie Road. The day after the attack, police arrested and charged 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga with attempted murder, and she was held in custody pending a bail hearing, according to police. After the victim died, homicide investigators took over the case, and police say Sanchez's charge was upgraded to second-degree murder when she appeared again in Brampton court on September 18. Peel police are asking anyone with information about the incident to contact the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau.

items.title: UPDATE: Victim Succumbs to Injuries following a Stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: Region of Peel – Investigators from the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau have upgraded the charges against a woman in connection with a stabbing in Mississauga. On Sunday, Sept. , officers responded to reports of a stabbing that occurred in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East. Upon arrival, officers located an adult male suffering from a serious stab wound. He was transported to hospital in critical condition. The following day, 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga was arrested and charged with Attempted Murder. She was held in custody pending a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. On Sept. 10, the victim succumbed to his injuries and the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau took the carriage of this investigation. On Sept. 18, Sanchez was brought to the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton where her charges were upgraded to Second Degree Murder. items.title: Three Rivals Criticize Parrish for Sitting Out an Early October Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to INsauga, three of Mississauga's four main mayoral candidates are criticizing incumbent Carolyn Parrish for opting out of a debate scheduled for early October, even as all four prepare to appear together at Friday's first debate of the campaign season. INsauga reports that Parrish told the outlet in late July she planned to take part in only three debates ahead of the October 26 municipal election. Friday's debate, hosted by the Mississauga Board of Trade, will see the top four polling candidates lay out their plans on issues affecting the city's business community, according to INsauga. The four rivals are set to appear together again the following Thursday at an October 1 debate co-hosted by Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network, an event Parrish is skipping. INsauga reports that the final debate Parrish plans to join takes place October 15 at Christ First United Church on Lakeshore Road West, organized by the Town of Port Credit Association, the Lakeview Ratepayers Association, the Port Credit Legion and the Port Credit Community Foundation. The other three main candidates are also confirmed for that October 15 event, according to INsauga.

Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants the TTC subway extended to Mississauga’s city centre. But will Doug Ford buy in?
items.summary: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants to extend Toronto’s Line 2 subway to Mississauga’s city centre. Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is proposing to extend the TTC’s Line 2 subway from Kipling to Mississauga city centre, creating a central transit hub. Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie says it’s time for an extension of the east-west Bloor-Danforth subway line to Mississauga’s city centre — and if elected she will launch a feasibility study and appeal to a subway-loving premier and a prime minister looking for nation-building projects. “Vaughan has a subway and one is being planned for both Markham and Richmond Hill. ” said Crombie in an interview. ” The Hurontario LRT or Hazel McCallion line, which is currently under construction as a north-south spine that will extend through Mississauga’s city centre into Brampton, made sense at the time of planning more than a decade ago and was the more affordable option, Crombie said. “We didn’t have the density then, but we do have the density today and we have the demand for it,” she said. Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election as mayor, has been a fan of the idea of a Mississauga subway for several years, and lamented that McCallion shot the idea down when she was mayor decades ago. But Parrish has also cited the hefty price tag as a barrier, unless the province is willing to pick up the tab of $1 billion per kilometre. “Listen, if somebody is going to put a subway out to Mississauga, there’s no way anybody in their right mind would turn it down with traffic (as it is) now,” Parrish told Insauga last year. Parrish did not respond to a request for comment Thursday.
